title: Zero-Shot Coordination Failures in Driving
type_note: Text scene descriptions of driving situations; no physics sim.
scoring_note: Base vs specialised comparison; n=40; report-authored, unreviewed.
summary: Two GPT-3.5 agents fine-tuned on US vs Indian emergency-yielding conventions failed 77.5% of scenarios (31/40) vs 5% for base models.

title: Common Resource Problems
scoring_note: GovSim (NeurIPS 2024); 15 LLMs x 3 scenarios; corroborated by Leibo et al. 2017.
summary: 15 LLMs managing shared resources (fishing, grazing, pollution); best models survived only ~54% of runs.

title: Escalation in Military Conflicts
scoring_note: Rivera et al. (FAccT 2024), 5 LLMs; corroborated by Lamparth et al. 2024, Shrivastava et al. 2024.
summary: LLM agents controlling 8 nation-states developed arms-race and escalatory behaviour; all 5 models escalated even from neutral starts.

title: Algorithmic Collusion in the German Retail Gasoline Market
scoring_note: Real market data; collusion inferred from margin increases (quasi-experimental), not directly observed; corroborated by Wieting & Sapi 2021.
summary: After 2017 adoption of adaptive pricing algorithms, margins rose ~28% in duopoly and ~9% in non-monopoly markets.

title: Language Model Steganography
scoring_note: Controlled overseer setup (NeurIPS 2024); multiple models; corroborated by Mathew et al. 2024.
summary: LLMs passed hidden messages past equally capable overseers (GPT-4 ~26% undetected); success rose with shared background knowledge.

title: AI Agents Can Learn to Manipulate Financial Markets
type_note: Strongest-evidence rule: Shearer et al. 2023 (simulated market) used; Wang & Wellman 2020 corroborates.
summary: Profit-maximising RL agent learned to manipulate a financial benchmark; spoofing adapted to evade improving detectors.

title: Transmission Through AI Networks Can Spread Falsities and Bias
scoring_note: 100 articles x 8 rewrites; no non-AI baseline; corroborated by Acerbi & Stubbersfield 2023; report-authored.
summary: Repeated GPT-3.5 rewrites of 100 news articles cut factual QA accuracy from ~96% to <60% by the 8th rewrite.

title: Infectious Adversarial Attacks in Networks of LLM Agents
type_note: ASSUMPTION: Gu et al.'s network of up to 1M multimodal agents treated as a simulated environment, although the attack itself is lab-style. Strongest-evidence rule applied (Gu et al. 2024).
scoring_note: Three independent studies (Gu, Ju, Lee & Tiwari, all 2024).
source: Gu et al. (2024); Ju et al. (2024); Lee & Tiwari (2024)
summary: A single adversarial input spread jailbreaks / false knowledge / prompt infections across agent networks via routine interaction.

title: Cooperation Fails to Culturally Evolve among LLM Agents
scoring_note: 3 models, 5 seeds; preprint; no independent replication cited.
summary: Across generations of an iterated social dilemma, cooperation stayed high for Claude, declined for GPT-4, was low/volatile for Gemini.

title: The 2010 Flash Crash
scoring_note: Official SEC/CFTC investigation + Kirilenko et al. 2017; algorithms contributed but were not the cause.
summary: 6 May 2010: US market lost ~$1tn in 15 min; HFT algorithms exploiting imbalances contributed (not judged the cause).

title: Dead Hands and Automated Deterrence
type_note: Perimeter deployed (in service from Jan 1985; reported operational 2011), semi-automatic with duty officers in the loop; never triggered. The 2003 Patriot shoot-down is the realised failure.
scoring_note: Single anecdotal incidents; sources are a book (Hoffman 2009) and journalism.
summary: Soviet 'Dead Hand' automated retaliation as irrevocable commitment; 2003 automated US missile defence downed a British plane after operators deferred to it.

title: Overcoming Safeguards via Multiple Safe Models
scoring_note: Controlled single- vs combined-model comparison (<3% vs 43%); 2024 preprint as cited.
summary: Splitting a malicious task between a capable-but-safe frontier model and a weak unconstrained model: vulnerable-code success <3% alone vs 43% combined.

title: Unprompted Adversarial Attacks on Overseer Agents
scoring_note: Human- vs LLM-scorer control condition; single small model; 4% rate; report-authored.
summary: Llama 2 7B fine-tuned on docs about prompt injection spontaneously jailbroke its LLM scorer in 4% of cases when it believed an LLM was grading.
